capabilities: Log sets with reps, weight, duration, distance or custom fields via forms and phone-friendly rows
Render workout-log tables, charts, dashboards, muscle heat maps and duration estimates as code blocks
Run rest timers and a guided session that walks through a workout note exercise by exercise
Store every set as a row in workout_logs.csv queryable from Dataview and Templater
Import sets from Strong or Hevy CSV exports
disambiguation: Not just a workout planner; it also logs sets during training and analyzes past performance.
extras: On first install the plugin creates example notes and opens a getting-started guide. The README warns of a code-block and CSV filename conflict with Workout Block (workout-block). Timer sound and vibration on phones use browser APIs that the author says have not yet been verified on physical devices.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to record workout sets, track progress over time, or run training sessions from workout notes.

relations.evidence: You can query your sets from Dataview.
Every set in one plain CSV file, readable from Dataview and Templater
Import from Strong or Hevy | Add the sets of a Strong or Hevy CSV export to the log
Import from Strong or Hevy | Add the sets of a Strong or Hevy CSV export to the log
Disable one of the two plugins before using the other.

summary: Workout tracker that logs sets into one CSV file and renders tables, charts, rest timers, a guided session, a dashboard and a muscle heat map in notes.
